raw_response:
I've been farming this land for 50 years. I know my 2.6 mu like I know my own hands. Cotton is all I grow — always has been. My wife and I don't need more than this, and at 73, I'm not learning something new.

I'll plough in late April once the soil has warmed enough. I always plough — turns the old stalks under, breaks up the hardpan. My father did it, I do it.

For seed, I'll use the improved Bt variety I switched to about 15 years ago. It handles the bollworm better so I don't have to spray as much for that. I buy from the same seed supplier in the county town every year.

Fertilizer: I spread base fertilizer before planting — some phosphorus and potassium mixed with compound fertilizer — then I topdress with urea during boll development in July and August. I don't use scales, but over the years I've learned roughly how much a bucket holds. About 16 jin of nitrogen equivalent per mu across the season feels right.

Irrigation: I pump from my well. I water before planting to get moisture into the seedbed, then again at squaring, flowering, and peak boll development. Four times is usually enough unless the summer is especially dry.

Pesticides: Even with Bt cotton, I still need to spray for aphids and spider mites. Usually five times through the season, watching the plants closely.

I expect around 280 kg of seed cotton per mu. Some years a little more, some less. At my age I'm not pushing for record yields — I just want a steady harvest.
